name: Bluish petrol
lede: Bluish petrol is a deep, muted teal-blue carried into our library from a Japanese traditional color name, and it sits only a short step from plain [[petrol]].

sections.title: Hanaasagi, a flower's light blue
sections.body:
Our library lists this color from the Wikipedia survey "Traditional colors of Japan," under the romanized name Hanaasagi, written 花浅葱 [1]. The kanji combine "flower" with a word for a pale, pale-indigo blue, and the library glosses the whole as "light blue flower" [1]. The books consulted for this project do not independently confirm a date or a specific flower, so the naming story beyond that gloss is undocumented here [1].

In our color library the nearest already-named neighbor is [[petrol]], a color-distance of 5.5 by the CIEDE2000 formula, close enough that most eyes would call them the same blue-green [1]. The hex given here, #1D697C, is a modern screen reading chosen to match that gloss; it is not a measurement of dyed cloth or any surviving object, so treat it as approximate [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
A color within range of this swatch appears in 68 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.29 percent, as photographed; a looser within-painting test finds it in 33 [2]. That makes it rarer than 56 percent of the named colors we track [2].

It peaks in the 1900s, present in 6 of 1,674 paintings from that century, 2.3 times the rate expected from the museums those works come from [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in a third of the paintings that carry it, the kind of tone that lightness alone would not single out [2]. The earliest dated appearance we have is Quentin Massys, 1500, though the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a true first sighting [2].

origin.named_after: flower blue, from 花 (flower) and 浅葱 (a pale indigo blue)
